summary.title: AMD Next-Generation "Zen 4" Core and 4th Gen AMD EPYC Server CPUs
summary.one_liner: Learn how AMD's Zen 4 core, built on Zen 3 with TSMC 5-nm technology, yields the 4th gen EPYC server lineup (Genoa, Genoa-X, Bergamo, Siena) and what gains it delivers.
keywords: how amd zen 4 improves on zen 3
takeaways: Zen 4 is AMD's latest x86 core, evolved from the Zen 3 microarchitecture and manufactured on TSMC's 5-nm technology.
Compared with Zen 3, Zen 4 is claimed to deliver 14% higher IPC, a 16% higher frequency at the same voltage, up to 60% less power at the same performance, and AVX-512 support.
Zen 4c targets power efficiency by using a lower boost frequency.

The 4th gen EPYC family uses chiplet architecture to tailor processors to market needs: Genoa and Genoa-X for performance, Bergamo for high core-count cloud, and Siena for a streamlined power-efficient form factor.
summary.summary: This IEEE Xplore paper, written by the AMD designers, describes the Zen 4 core and the 4th gen AMD EPYC server processor family built on it. It covers how Zen 4 evolved from Zen 3 on TSMC 5-nm technology and the four claimed improvements: IPC, frequency at the same voltage, power at the same performance, and AVX-512 support. It also introduces the chiplet-based product line of Genoa, Genoa-X, Bergamo and Siena. The page shows only the abstract and an endnote reference, so the technical detail beyond that is not visible here.
